scenes.title: The first message
scenes.text: In 1969, scientists sent the first message between two computers. The network was ARPANET, and it crashed after two letters.

scenes.title: The first email
scenes.text: In 1971, Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email, and chose the at sign for addresses.

scenes.title: Birth of the internet
scenes.text: In 1983, ARPANET adopted a shared language called TCP IP. Many call this the birth of the internet.

scenes.title: The World Wide Web
scenes.text: In 1991, Tim Berners-Lee opened the first website to the public. The web made the internet easy for everyone.

scenes.title: People online
scenes.text: In 2005, about one billion people were online. By 2025, six billion. Almost three quarters of the world.

scenes.title: Social media
scenes.text: Then social media took off. Facebook in 2004, YouTube in 2005, and Twitter in 2006.

scenes.title: Internet in your pocket
scenes.text: In 2007, the iPhone put the internet in every pocket. Apps and streaming followed.

scenes.title: What comes next?
scenes.text: Today, satellites and AI are changing it again. What comes next? Tell me in the comments.
